summary:
Earth Observatory is a web application that turns official NASA and NOAA data into an interactive experience for understanding how our planet is changing. A 3D globe lets you explore temperature anomalies (NASA GISTEMP), atmospheric CO₂ (NOAA GML), and Arctic and Antarctic sea ice (NOAA/NSIDC) since 1880, with regional charts and a year player.

It tackles the challenge in two ways. First, it makes the data understandable: a "detective" answers questions typed or spoken, in English or Spanish, and explains each trend along with its statistical significance and limits. Second, it protects trust: it uses only real data, updates every 12 hours, and if a source fails, it says so and shows the last real download without inventing values. Its methodology is public.

It matters because climate decisions rely on evidence, yet that evidence often stays locked in hard-to-read tables. The app brings it to anyone, even on a phone and with accessibility aids.
details: What does it do and how does it work? Earth Observatory is a web application featuring an interactive 3D globe that you can rotate and explore. It uses real data from NASA and NOAA to show how much the planet has warmed, the atmospheric CO₂ levels, and the remaining sea ice in the Arctic and Antarctic. The server checks for new data every 12 hours. If a source fails, the app notifies users and continues displaying the last valid download. You can use a year slider to watch how everything changes, search for a country or ocean, and view regional charts that include events like El Niño. You can also talk to a "detective": ask a question by typing or by voice, in English or Spanish, and it answers using only the data loaded in the app. Whenever a trend is displayed, it indicates whether it is statistically significant or if there is insufficient data to claim so. Benefits It transforms complex scientific tables into something visual, interactive, and easy to understand, allowing users to ask questions about the data by text or voice. It is also completely transparent: the Methodology tab details the origin, calculation method, and limitations of every data point. It works on mobile phones and includes accessibility options for a more comfortable reading experience. Expected Impact We want students and anyone with curiosity to be able to verify for themselves how the climate is changing, without needing to be experts. By showing the exact origin of each data point and its level of certainty, the app helps transform abstract numbers into tangible evidence that can be understood and questioned. Tools - Backend/Server: Python with Flask, pandas, and NumPy. - Frontend: JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, using globe.gl (Three.js) for the 3D globe and Plotly for the charts. - Services: Gemini for the "detective" and Open-Meteo for current weather and location search. - Deployment/Hosting: Render, with Git and GitHub. - Data sources: NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GML, and NOAA/NSIDC. No special hardware required. Use of AI Code, writing, and interface design were developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic), under the team's direction and review. The app's "detective" generates its responses using Gemini (Google), strictly based on the official data loaded into the application. Climate data (temperature, CO₂, ice) comes directly from NASA and NOAA, so it was neither generated nor fabricated by AI. AI assisted with the interface design; no AI-generated images are shown in the app or in the presentation. What makes it creative? Instead of a traditional dashboard of charts, it features a virtual "detective" you can type or speak to, which guides you through the data. It always displays exact data traceability (where the data comes from and when it was last verified), keeps working with locally saved data if the connection fails, and has a distinctive dark style with bright neon colors that feels modern and comfortable to use on a phone. What the team took into account - Using exclusively official and real data, avoiding fabricated values or mock examples. - Scientific rigor: statistical significance, clear baselines, and explicit warnings when data is missing or sources fail. - Resilience against external source outages. - A smooth mobile experience. - An accessible conversational interface by text and voice.
